text:
arya: FYI Argus-10b went to 10% canary last night. Seeing two things: 1) short-code completions frequently truncate mid-token, 2) p99 latency creeps after ~8k total tokens served in a worker. :thinking_face:
mika: saw the truncation on the code tests too. It looks like token boundaries are different vs our prod tokenizer — some SP pieces split differently.
sanjay: can you paste an example?
arya: example: input `def fib(n):` expected continuation starts with `    if n < 2:` but output was `    if n <` then stop. Log shows last token in response is `n` not `n:`.
owen: do we have tokenization map used during model conversion? maybe bpe merges were adjusted during quant pipeline.
jen: I ran `eval-bench` on the canary set, perplexity +6% vs baseline on code subset, embeddings similarity for snippet matching down ~0.03 cos. eval-bot: automated eval pings: code-suite regressions: perplexity +5.9%, top-k exact match down 4.1%.
mika: interestingly CPU memory on the worker increases slowly over time (heap growth) — after ~7k served tokens process RSS +120MB. Could be kv-cache retention bug when using quantized attention kernels.
sanjay: steps proposed: 1) stop canary ramp, 2) run canary with original tokenizer artifact (from model tar) pinned, 3) run memory profiler on runtime with same traffic replay. Agree?
arya: +1 to stopping ramp. I already set canary to 0% and put rollback flag in rollout console. deploy-bot: rollback initiated for rollout argus-10b-canary -> previous stable model at 2024-11-02T03:21Z. :white_check_mark:
owen: for the tokenizer mismatch I suspect the conversion script `convert_sp_model.py` we used added --drop-unk or re-serialized merges. Quick test: compare token ids for `if n < 2:` between source SP and converted SP:
```
# py
from sentencepiece import SentencePieceProcessor
src = SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='argus_orig.model')
conv = SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='argus_converted.model')
print(src.encode('    if n < 2:'))
print(conv.encode('    if n < 2:'))
```

mika: good call, I'll run that tonight against the canary artifact. Also will add a short unit test to the conversion pipeline to assert idempotence for the top 1k frequent tokens.
sanjay: for the memory growth I'll instrument runtime with heap snapshots (jemalloc stats + pprof) and enable an internal gauge that triggers a trace at +50MB since baseline. Owen can you own that?
owen: on it. I'll also disable continuous KV caching for argus in config to see if it stabilizes.
jen: we should also run a small q-aware decode test: quantized kernels sometimes truncate when last logits are very small (rounding). Can you run deterministic sampling vs float32 emulation?
mika: will run decode with `--emulate-fp32` flag on the quant runner. If it repros only in quant mode that's telling.
jen: thanks. Also adding a quick eval: run 500 code completions with golden suffix and compute suffix-prediction F1 to triage quality loss.
arya: timeline: rollback done, someone owns tokenizer id diff (mika), someone instruments memory (owen), someone runs fp32 emulation (mika), research team to produce small root-cause PR by EOD tomorrow. I can coordinate with support for any customer-facing notes.
sanjay: noted. I'll create an incident ticket and link the logs.
arya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
